Choose the workstream

One legal category. Different jobs to get done.

An exchange founder, a game studio and a tokenized-fund manager may all search for a crypto lawyer. They are not buying the same legal service. One needs a market-entry and customer-asset model, another needs token and intellectual-property advice, and the third needs offering documents that match an investor register. Start with what the business actually does and the decisions the legal team must help it make.

Describe who controls the product and contracts, who holds assets or keys, who receives money, which users can participate and which markets the service targets. Include planned functions, not only the narrow version in the current demo. Ask candidates to identify dependencies and specialist involvement rather than compress every issue into a generic compliance package.

Match the proposed team to the business activity
MandateCapabilities to discussOutput to request
Exchanges and tradingFinancial regulation, market structure, custody, AML and customer termsActivity and jurisdiction map; permissions work plan; customer-asset responsibilities
Stablecoins and paymentsBanking/payments, redemption, reserves and distributionIssuer and payment-flow analysis; role allocation; documents and operating conditions
DeFi and DAOsProtocol design, governance, corporate, regulatory and taxControl and activity assessment; entity and contributor arrangements; governance decisions
Token launches and fundraisingCorporate, securities, distribution, communications and taxRights and distribution analysis; transaction documents; launch conditions
Wallets and custodyAsset control, customer contracts, privacy and recoveryAccount/key model; failure procedures; provider agreements
NFTs, gaming and communitiesIP, consumer terms, commercial contracts and dataRights and licensing model; platform terms; content and brand permissions
Funds and tokenized assetsFunds, asset law, securities, custody and servicingOffering and record structure; investor restrictions; lifecycle documents
Disputes and investigationsLitigation, enforcement, insolvency and forensicsPreservation and instruction plan; representation scope; coordinated response

This matrix scopes a conversation, not a legal classification. The same business can occupy several rows. Ask the lead lawyer which facts are needed before advice can be given and which questions require another specialist.

Beyond tokenization

Scope the product before asking for a legal conclusion

Exchanges, brokers and trading infrastructure

Explain order handling, execution, settlement, balances, custody, fiat partners and market-making relationships. Include intended derivatives, leverage or lending functions. Identify which entity performs each activity rather than giving counsel only screenshots of the interface.

Request a work plan separating the operator from its custodian, payment provider, affiliated issuer and trading counterparties. A counterparty's authorization does not answer questions about your own role. Document customer terms, complaints and failed-transaction responsibilities. An application, regulator discussion, authorization and continuing permission condition are different events; avoid promising outcomes the project has not obtained.

Stablecoins, payments and settlement

Show the money-flow diagram: payment method, entities receiving funds, conversion, token movement, settlement and redemption. Using another issuer's stablecoin is a different model from issuing your own instrument. Ask who owes redemption, who controls funds in transit and who handles delays or rejected payments.

The legal team should work with banking, payments and compliance owners on the proposed arrangement. A successful API integration does not settle permissions or commercial terms. Changing the issuer, reserve arrangement, provider or user countries can change the assumptions behind earlier advice.

DeFi, DAOs and governance

Supply facts about upgrade keys, emergency powers, fees, treasury decisions, interface access and governance execution. A decentralized label is not a substitute for the control model. Separate developers, an operating company, foundation, contributors and token holders, and clarify who the legal client is.

Ask who signs contracts, employs contributors and handles disputes. A community vote, an administrator action and a binding obligation are not automatically the same thing. Useful outputs include a responsibility map, governance and contributor documents, and a list of changes needing renewed advice.

Tokens, NFTs, games and intellectual property

Bring the token rights, distribution plan, rewards, marketing material and proposed partners. Ask for analysis of the actual facts rather than a conclusion based only on a token standard or utility label. Include later transfers and incentives in the brief.

For NFTs and games, identify artwork, brands, software and licensed content. Token ownership does not by itself establish copyright ownership. Ask how the customer promise matches the license and terms. Scope development, hosting, minting, marketplace and distribution agreements, including IP, security responsibilities, termination and continuity.

Wallets and customer-asset control

Document ordinary and exceptional asset movement: user signatures, administrator rights, recovery, third-party signers and support procedures. Do not infer legal treatment from technical phrases such as MPC, smart account or non-custodial. The customer interface, key-control provider and underlying asset holder may be different entities.

Walk through a compromised account, disputed instruction, frozen transaction and provider shutdown. Ask who can authorize action, what evidence is needed and which record is authoritative. Counsel and engineering should agree what must be documented and tested.

Funds, RWA issuance and servicing

A fund investing in crypto is not necessarily the same project as a fund whose own interests are tokenized. Likewise, an SPV interest is different from putting a property's legal title onchain. Identify the rights and instrument before comparing firms.

Use the separate tokenization law firms guide for offshore fund counsel, asset-specific briefing, investor records, issuance and servicing. This directory remains the wider discovery page for crypto and Web3 legal needs.

Complete the mandate

Tax, privacy, disputes and operational responsibilities

Tax and transaction structuring

Identify the issuer or operating company, founders, employees, contributors and customer groups, and explain which token, payment or investment events are planned. Ask which tax specialists and jurisdictions are included. Token issuance, compensation, treasury activity and investor reporting are different questions. Do not assume a general regulatory memo covers tax or that another participant's treatment applies to your entity.

Privacy, security and technology agreements

Map personal data, analytics, KYC records, wallet identifiers and vendors. Describe where information is stored and who can access it. Ask counsel and the relevant specialists to assess the actual architecture rather than making broad assumptions about blockchain anonymity. Include retention, access, incident response and termination obligations in provider contracts.

Review open-source use, IP ownership, development and node-service agreements. Where Web3 intersects with AI, identify model/API providers, training inputs, generated content and data sharing. These facts help the team identify the appropriate specialists; they do not by themselves decide the legal result.

Investigations, breaches and disputes

If the immediate problem is a regulatory inquiry, hacked wallet, contract dispute or provider insolvency, say that first. This differs from a new-product mandate. Establish who may instruct counsel, relevant deadlines and whether litigation, insolvency, regulatory or forensic specialists are needed. Do not assume product counsel includes emergency representation.

Preserve potentially relevant agreements, communications, transaction references and logs, and agree a secure sharing process. Never send seed phrases or private keys to a purported recovery service. Distinguish tracing from recovery and an allegation from an established finding. A forensic report is not a guarantee of a remedy, counterparty cooperation or money being returned.

Fundraising, acquisitions and corporate work

Identify which entity raises capital, grants rights or signs the transaction. Explain any token rights alongside equity, warrants or other arrangements. Ask which corporate, regulatory and tax workstreams are included and whether buyer, seller, issuer, founders and investors have different interests. Public deal experience should be checked for the proposed team's actual role, not only the firm name attached to a press release.

Check the boundaries

Match the legal entity, lawyer and local law

Map the operating company, users, investors, asset location, marketing channels and major service providers separately. An international office network does not prove local-law coverage for every activity. Ask the lead partner to identify the laws covered, separate counsel needed and who consolidates the advice. Request named lawyers and an engagement entity, not only a firm brand.

Use the appropriate professional register for the lawyer and practice. The SRA Solicitors Register is one example for England and Wales. The FCA Financial Services Register concerns a different check of financial firms, permissions and restrictions. Neither establishes specialist expertise or endorses a project. Check the exact entity, scope and date and use the relevant local equivalent elsewhere.

For an EU-facing product, ask counsel to determine the applicable framework from the rights and activities, not assume MiCA applies to every token. ESMA's MiCA resources distinguish the framework and register scope, including financial-instrument boundaries and the absence of regulator approval for listed white papers. For India, the US, UK, UAE, Singapore or Hong Kong, request analysis of the actual local activities instead of importing another market's answer.

Before sharing detailed materials, establish the conflict-check and confidentiality process. Confirm who the client is, who supervises the work and who can rely on advice. Coordinators, fractional counsel, incorporation services, compliance tools and forensic providers may help delivery, but those labels alone do not establish lawyer admission, privilege or authority to advise on every law involved.

Compare proposals

Send the same brief. Ask for accountable answers.

Prepare a plain-language product description, entity chart and diagram of money, assets, data and control. Include target users and markets, current contracts, providers, planned features and launch dependencies. State undecided facts clearly rather than hiding them behind globally compliant or fully decentralized language.

  1. Which legal entity engages us, and who is the accountable partner and day-to-day contact?
  2. Which comparable matters did the proposed team handle, and what was its actual role?
  3. Which activities, laws and jurisdictions are included or excluded?
  4. Which facts are needed before the team can give the requested advice?
  5. Which written deliverables will we receive and who can rely on them?
  6. Which regulatory, corporate, tax, IP, privacy and disputes specialists are involved?
  7. Who reviews provider contracts and resolves gaps in operating responsibility?
  8. How will advice become clear product, engineering and compliance decisions?
  9. Which changes trigger renewed review and who approves scope changes?
  10. How are conflicts, secure sharing, retention and confidentiality managed?
  11. What dependencies could change the sequence or delay implementation?
  12. What post-launch and incident support is included?

Compare completeness against the mandate, not office counts, awards or contact-database size. An opinion, transaction execution, ongoing product advice and dispute representation are different engagements. Maintain a decision record with the requirement, owner, evidence, exclusions and follow-up question. This supports a reasoned shortlist without invented expertise scores.

Warning signs include no named lawyer, unexplained engagement entities, blanket worldwide-compliance claims, guaranteed approvals and unclear local-counsel responsibilities. A proposal that states assumptions and exclusions can be easier to manage than one promising everything.

Make the advice usable

From legal work to operating evidence

Before launch, bring legal, compliance, product, engineering, security and operations into the same review. Trace the normal customer journey and the exceptions. Link each requirement to its responsible owner, document or policy and implementation evidence. A legal opinion does not establish secure code, and an audit does not decide legal rights or permissions.

Practical handover scenarios
ScenarioDecision to allocateEvidence to discuss
Rejected or restricted customerWho decides and what happens to pending money or assets?Onboarding controls, payment exception and customer communication
Conflicting asset recordsWhich record is authoritative and who investigates?Reconciliation, correction and escalation workflow
Compromised wallet or administratorWho can act, on what evidence and within which role?Recovery approvals, access logs and incident plan
New product or providerWhich earlier assumptions require another review?Change register, contract assessment and revised controls
Expansion into another countryWho assesses distribution and operating activities?Local review and documented launch conditions
Interruption or terminationHow can necessary servicing and record access continue?Export, notice, support and continuity arrangements

These are prompts for the responsible professionals, not conclusions about a particular transaction. Keep a dated record of facts supplied, advice assumptions, system versions, approvals and open decisions. Assign an owner for change monitoring after launch. New features, token rights, custody arrangements, user countries or governance powers can require another conversation.

Restrict confidential advice to appropriate recipients and avoid publishing it in project repositories or marketing materials. Agree retention and sharing with counsel. The objective is an operating team that can use the advice correctly, not a legal memo disconnected from the live product.

Build a shortlist around your actual business

Share the activity, target markets and immediate legal workstream. Keep confidential documents out of the initial enquiry and agree a sharing process with the responsible recipient.

Questions buyers ask

Crypto and Web3 legal FAQs

Which crypto or Web3 law firm is best?

There is no universal best firm. Match the named team to the actual activity, jurisdictions and lifecycle events. Compare relevant matters, engagement entities, local-law coverage, conflicts, written deliverables and implementation support rather than a generic ranking.

What does a crypto and Web3 law firm do?

The mandate can include exchanges, payments, token launches, DeFi and DAOs, custody, fundraising, IP, privacy, tax, transactions, investigations or disputes. Tokenization is one specialist workstream, not the whole category.

Does a global law firm cover every jurisdiction?

Do not assume so. Confirm the contracting entity, admitted lawyers and laws covered for your operating company, users, investors and distribution. Ask the lead partner to allocate separate local-counsel work in writing.

How do I check a lawyer or financial provider?

Check the exact lawyer and legal practice through the appropriate professional register. Financial-provider authorization is a separate check of permissions and restrictions. Neither registration nor a directory listing proves specialist experience or suitability for your project.

Can a legal consultant or platform replace a law firm?

Coordinators, compliance tools and platforms can support delivery, but identify who gives jurisdiction-specific legal advice and accepts responsibility. Do not infer admission, privilege or regulatory authorization from a service label.

Is tokenization legal work different from general Web3 advice?

A tokenized fund, bond or property offering may need asset, funds, securities, custody, investor-record and servicing specialists. An exchange, payment service or protocol can require a different combination. Use the separate tokenization-law guide for issuer-specific diligence.

Does a code audit settle the legal questions?

No. A technical audit reviews a defined system and scope. Legal analysis concerns rights, activities and responsibilities. Ask legal and engineering to reconcile the requirements with the implemented controls.

Can a firm guarantee approval or recovery?

No outcome should be assumed. Regulatory processes, disputes and asset recovery depend on facts, applicable law, counterparties and evidence. Treat guaranteed approval or guaranteed recovery claims as a reason for additional diligence.

Sources and scope

How to use this directory

The page combines existing directory discovery records with buyer guidance and current primary practice checks. Public descriptions establish what firms say they offer, not independent proof of expertise, availability or every local-law capability. Do not read an editorial update date as a new verification of every historical listing.

Current practice checks cover A&O Shearman, Ashurst Perkins Coie, Baker McKenzie, Clifford Chance, Davis Polk, DLA Piper, Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer, Latham & Watkins, Ogier, Sidley and Skadden. Firm identities, contracts and historical matters must be matched to the relevant legal entity and team. Inclusion does not grant a FluidRWA Vetted badge.

Use the tokenization law firms guide for RWA-specific work, or compare adjacent custody, KYC and AML, and security review providers. Those services have different responsibilities from legal counsel.
